fanoutqa_029612.x:
Peking University :: part 02 :: chunk_0001
Founded in 1898 as the **Imperial University** **of Peking** by royal charter from the [Guangxu Emperor](/wiki/Guangxu_Emperor "Guangxu Emperor"), it was China's first national university. In its early years, it also served as the highest administrative authority for education in China.[[4]](#cite_note-4) In May 1912, the [government of the Republic of China](/wiki/Government_of_the_Republic_of_China "Government of the Republic of China") ordered the Imperial University of Peking to be renamed Peking University. Then Peking University merged with [Yenching University](/wiki/Yenching_University "Yenching University") during the nationwide restructuring of universities and academic departments in 1952. In April 2000, the [Beijing Medical University](/wiki/Beijing_Medical_University "Beijing Medical University") merged with the Peking University.[[5]](#cite_note-ABOUT-PKU_HISTORY-5)

Peking University has eight faculties, namely Sciences, Informatics, Engineering, Humanities, Social Sciences, Economics and Management, Interdisciplinary as well as Health Science. It consists of 55 schools and departments, 24 research entities, and six affiliated hospitals.[[2]](#cite_note-pdf-2) By 2024, Peking University's staff included 54 academicians of the [Chinese Academy of Sciences](/wiki/Chinese_Academy_of_Sciences "Chinese Academy of Sciences"), 16 academicians of the [Chinese Academy of Engineering](/wiki/Chinese_Academy_of_Engineering "Chinese Academy of Engineering") and 20 members of the [World Academy of Sciences](/wiki/The_World_Academy_of_Sciences "The World Academy of Sciences").[[2]](#cite_note-pdf-2)

fanoutqa_025772.x:
Cleveland Cavaliers :: part 02 :: chunk_0001
The Cavaliers opened their inaugural season by losing their first 15 games and struggled in their early years, placing no better than sixth in the Eastern Conference during their first five seasons. The team won their first Central Division title in 1976, which also marked the first winning season and playoff appearance in franchise history, where they advanced to the Eastern Conference Finals. The franchise was purchased by [Ted Stepien](/wiki/Ted_Stepien "Ted Stepien") in 1980. Stepien's tenure as owner was marked by six coaching changes, questionable trades and [draft](/wiki/NBA_draft "NBA draft") decisions, and poor attendance, leading to $15 million in financial losses. The Cavs went 66–180 over the course of those three seasons and endured a 24-game losing streak spanning the 1981–82 and 1982–83 seasons.

[George](/wiki/George_Gund_III "George Gund III") and [Gordon Gund](/wiki/Gordon_Gund "Gordon Gund") purchased the franchise in 1983. During the latter half of the 1980s and through much of the 1990s, the Cavs were a regular playoff contender – led by players such as [Mark Price](/wiki/Mark_Price "Mark Price") and [Brad Daugherty](/wiki/Brad_Daugherty_(basketball) "Brad Daugherty (basketball)") – and advanced to the Eastern Conference Finals in 1992. After the team's playoff appearance in the 1997–98 season, however, the Cavs had six consecutive losing seasons with no playoff action. Cleveland was awarded with the top overall pick in the [2003 draft](/wiki/2003_NBA_draft "2003 NBA draft"), and they selected [LeBron James](/wiki/LeBron_James "LeBron James"). Behind James and [Zydrunas Ilgauskas](/wiki/Zydrunas_Ilgauskas "Zydrunas Ilgauskas"), the Cavaliers again became a regular playoff contender by 2005. They made their first appearance in the [NBA Finals](/wiki/NBA_Finals "NBA Finals") in [2007](/wiki/2007_NBA_Finals "2007 NBA Finals") after winning the first Eastern Conference championship in franchise history. Main article: [United Nations Security Council veto power](/wiki/United_Nations_Security_Council_veto_power "United Nations Security Council veto power")

See also: [List of vetoed United Nations Security Council resolutions](/wiki/List_of_vetoed_United_Nations_Security_Council_resolutions "List of vetoed United Nations Security Council resolutions")

Under [Article 27](/wiki/United_Nations_Security_Council_veto_power#UN_Charter "United Nations Security Council veto power") of the UN Charter, Security Council decisions on all substantive matters require the affirmative votes of nine members. A negative vote – or "veto" – by a permanent member prevents adoption of a proposal, even if it has received the required number of votes.[[75]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFasulo200440–41-77) Abstention is not regarded as a veto in most cases, though all five permanent members must actively concur to adopt any amendment to the Charter.[[64]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFomerand2009287-66) Procedural matters cannot be vetoed, nor can the veto be used to prevent discussion of an issue. The same holds for certain non-binding decisions that directly regard permanent members.[[75]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEFasulo200440–41-77) Most vetoes have been used for blocking a candidate for Secretary-General or the admission of a member state, not in critical international security situations.[[80]](#cite_note-Veto-83)

In the negotiations leading to the creation of the UN, the veto power was opposed by many smaller countries and was in effect imposed by the five sponsoring powers, who made clear that the UN would not be founded without it. In 1982, inspired by [John Carpenter](/wiki/John_Carpenter "John Carpenter")'s horror film *[Halloween](/wiki/Halloween_(1978_film) "Halloween (1978 film)")* (1978),[[22]](#cite_note-22) as well as a nightmare about an invincible robot hit-man sent from the future to assassinate him,[[23]](#cite_note-23) Cameron wrote the script for *[The Terminator](/wiki/The_Terminator "The Terminator")* (1984), a sci-fi action film about a [cyborg](/wiki/Cyborg "Cyborg") sent from the future to carry out a lethal mission. Cameron wanted to sell the script so that he could direct the film. While some film studios expressed interest in the project, many executives were unwilling to let a new and unfamiliar director make the film. [Gale Anne Hurd](/wiki/Gale_Anne_Hurd "Gale Anne Hurd"), a colleague and founder of [Pacific Western Productions](/wiki/Valhalla_Entertainment "Valhalla Entertainment"), agreed to buy Cameron's script for one dollar, on the condition that Cameron direct the film. He convinced the president of [Hemdale Pictures](/wiki/Hemdale_Film_Corporation "Hemdale Film Corporation") to make the film, with Cameron as director and Hurd as a producer. [Lance Henriksen](/wiki/Lance_Henriksen "Lance Henriksen"), who starred in *Piranha II: The Spawning*, was considered for the lead role, but Cameron decided that [Arnold Schwarzenegger](/wiki/Arnold_Schwarzenegger "Arnold Schwarzenegger") was more suitable as the cyborg villain due to his [bodybuilder](/wiki/Bodybuilder "Bodybuilder") appearance.[[24]](#cite_note-Futurist-24) Henriksen was given a smaller role instead. [Michael Biehn](/wiki/Michael_Biehn "Michael Biehn") and [Linda Hamilton](/wiki/Linda_Hamilton "Linda Hamilton") also joined the cast. *The Terminator* was a box office success, exceeding expectations set by [Orion Pictures](/wiki/Orion_Pictures "Orion Pictures"),[[24]](#cite_note-Futurist-24) and earning over $78 milli

Napoleon :: Early life :: chunk_0004
Napoleon's family was of Italian origin. His paternal ancestors, the Buonapartes, descended from a minor [Tuscan](/wiki/Tuscany "Tuscany") noble family who emigrated to [Corsica](/wiki/Corsica "Corsica") in the 16th century. His maternal ancestors, the Ramolinos, descended from a noble family from [Lombardy](/wiki/Lombardy_(historical_region) "Lombardy (historical region)").[[12]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMcLynn19972-15) Napoleon's parents, [Carlo Maria Buonaparte](/wiki/Carlo_Buonaparte "Carlo Buonaparte") and [Maria Letizia Ramolino](/wiki/Letizia_Bonaparte "Letizia Bonaparte"), lived in the [Maison Bonaparte](/wiki/Maison_Bonaparte "Maison Bonaparte") in [Ajaccio](/wiki/Ajaccio "Ajaccio"), where Napoleon was born on 15 August 1769. He had an elder brother, [Joseph](/wiki/Joseph_Bonaparte "Joseph Bonaparte"), and six younger siblings: [Lucien](/wiki/Lucien_Bonaparte "Lucien Bonaparte"), [Elisa](/wiki/Elisa_Bonaparte "Elisa Bonaparte"), [Louis](/wiki/Louis_Bonaparte "Louis Bonaparte"), [Pauline](/wiki/Pauline_Bonaparte "Pauline Bonaparte"), [Caroline](/wiki/Caroline_Bonaparte "Caroline Bonaparte"), and [Jérôme](/wiki/J%C3%A9r%C3%B4me_Bonaparte "Jérôme Bonaparte").[[13]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEZamoyski2018xiv,_14-16) Five more siblings were stillborn or did not survive infancy.[[14]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMcLynn19974-17) Napoleon was baptized as a [Catholic](/wiki/Catholic_Church "Catholic Church") under the name *Napoleone di Buonaparte*. In his youth, his name was also spelled as *Nabulione*, *Nabulio*, *Napolionne*, and *Napulione*.[[15]](#cite_note-dwyerxv2-18)

Napoleon was born one year after the [Republic of Genoa](/wiki/Republic_of_Genoa "Republic of Genoa") ceded Corsica to France through the [Treaty of Versailles](/wiki/Treaty_of_Versailles_(1768) "Treaty of Versailles (1768)").[[16]](#cite_note-McLynn-1997b-19)[[d]](#cite_note-23) His father supported [Pasquale Paoli](/wiki/Pasquale_Paoli "Pasquale Paoli") during the [Corsican war

At West Point, Eisenhower relished the emphasis on traditions and on sports, but was less enthusiastic about the hazing, though he willingly accepted it as a plebe. He was also a regular violator of the more detailed regulations and finished school with a less than stellar discipline rating. Academically, Eisenhower's best subject by far was English. Otherwise, his performance was average, though he thoroughly enjoyed the typical emphasis of engineering on science and mathematics.[[26]](#cite_note-27)

In athletics, Eisenhower later said that "not making the baseball team at West Point was one of the greatest disappointments of my life, maybe my greatest".[[27]](#cite_note-rayaip-28) He made the [varsity football team](/wiki/Army_Black_Knights_football "Army Black Knights football")[[28]](#cite_note-ameddregiment.amedd.army.mil-29)[[29]](#cite_note-ameddregiment.amedd.army.mil_2-30) and was a starter at [halfback](/wiki/Halfback_(American_football) "Halfback (American football)") in 1912, when he tried to tackle the legendary [Jim Thorpe](/wiki/Jim_Thorpe "Jim Thorpe") of the [Carlisle Indians](/wiki/Carlisle_Indians_football "Carlisle Indians football").[[30]](#cite_note-31) Eisenhower suffered a torn knee while being tackled in the next game, which was the last he played; he reinjured his knee on horseback and in the boxing ring,[[4]](#cite_note-barnett19421109-5)[[13]](#cite_note-ease-14)[[31]](#cite_note-32) so he turned to fencing and gymnastics.[[4]](#cite_note-barnett19421109-5)

Eisenhower later served as junior varsity football coach and cheerleader, which caught the attention of General [Frederick Funston](/wiki/Frederick_Funston "Frederick Funston").[[32]](#cite_note-Team_America-33) He graduated from West Point in the middle of the class of 1915,[[33]](#cite_note-34) which became known as "[the class the stars fell on](/wiki/The_class_the_stars_fell_on "The class the stars fell on"

With a total of 32 domestic honours, Milan is one of the most successful clubs in Italy. The club won its first Serie A title in 1901 with its most recent coming in 2022. Milan's tenth *[scudetto](/wiki/List_of_Italian_football_champions "List of Italian football champions")* win meant that it earned the right to place a [star](/wiki/Star_(football_badge) "Star (football badge)") on its jersey in recognition of this.

Milan is the most successful Italian club in [international football](/wiki/AC_Milan_in_European_football "AC Milan in European football") with 20 major international trophies won (18 of them organised by UEFA and FIFA), and the third most successful in Europe overall after Real Madrid and Barcelona. They have won the European Cup/Champions League seven times, an Italian record and only surpassed by Real Madrid, with their most recent coming in 2007. Milan's fifth European Cup win, in 1994, meant that the club was [awarded the trophy permanently](/wiki/European_Champion_Clubs%27_Cup "European Champion Clubs' Cup") and is allowed to display a [multiple-winner badge](/wiki/UEFA_badge_of_honour "UEFA badge of honour") on its shirt.[[99]](#cite_note-102) The club also holds a joint record of two wins in the Latin Cup and a joint record of three wins in the Intercontinental Cup. **Tokyo**,[[a]](#cite_note-10) officially the **Tokyo Metropolis**,[[b]](#cite_note-11) is the [capital](/wiki/Capital_of_Japan "Capital of Japan") and [most populous city](/wiki/List_of_cities_in_Japan "List of cities in Japan") of [Japan](/wiki/Japan "Japan"). With a population of over 14 million in the [city proper](/wiki/City_proper "City proper") in 2023, it is [one of the most populous urban areas in the world](/wiki/List_of_largest_cities "List of largest cities"). The [Greater Tokyo Area](/wiki/Greater_Tokyo_Area "Greater Tokyo Area"), which includes Tokyo and parts of six neighboring [prefectures](/wiki/Prefectures_of_Japan "Prefectures of Japan"), is the most populous metropolitan area in the world, with 41 million residents as of 2024.

Lying at the head of [Tokyo Bay](/wiki/Tokyo_Bay "Tokyo Bay"), Tokyo is part of the [Kantō region](/wiki/Kant%C5%8D_region "Kantō region"), on the central coast of [Honshu](/wiki/Honshu "Honshu"), Japan's largest island. It is Japan's economic center and the seat of the [Japanese government](/wiki/Government_of_Japan "Government of Japan") and the [Emperor of Japan](/wiki/Emperor_of_Japan "Emperor of Japan"). The [Tokyo Metropolitan Government](/wiki/Tokyo_Metropolitan_Government "Tokyo Metropolitan Government") administers Tokyo's central [23 special wards](/wiki/Special_wards_of_Tokyo "Special wards of Tokyo"), which formerly made up [Tokyo City](/wiki/Tokyo_City "Tokyo City"); various commuter towns and suburbs in [its western area](/wiki/Western_Tokyo "Western Tokyo"); and two outlying island chains, the [Tokyo Islands](/wiki/Tokyo_Islands "Tokyo Islands").
